sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1975. South-Eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 613-666. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-C38.613
sources.note: Nothing on O'oku. The only prosodic remark is phylum-wide, p.622 (2.9.3.1 Phonological aspects): 'Some languages are tonal but stress is generally important and related to intonation which may be quite complex.' -- a generalisation over all South-East TNG Phylum languages, not attributable to O'oku; p.643: 'None of the [Mailuan] languages except Magi (or Mailu) has been studied or recorded in any detail.'

sources.citation: Pawley, A. & H. Hammarstrom. 2017. The Trans New Guinea family. In B. Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton (OAPEN open-access chapter).
sources.note: Nothing. p.65: 'O'oku, a poorly attested and now extinct language also appears to be Mailuan, closest to Bauwaki (Ray 1938)'; listing 'O'oku [-] 0; wordlist: Ray 1938'.

sources.citation: Dutton, T. 1982. Borrowing in Austronesian and non-Austronesian languages of coastal south-east mainland Papua New Guinea. PL C-74:109-177.
sources.note: Nothing; fn.11: 'the former community of O'oku (the whereabouts of whose members is not known) seems to have been originally a Yareban communalect with heavy borrowing from Laua and/or Magi'.

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1976. Magori and similar languages of South-East Papua. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 2, 581-636. PL C-39.
sources.note: Nothing on O'oku phonology. p.585: Strong (1911a) 'published short lists for Laua and O'oku, a village "somewhere to the west of Laua"'; p.617: O'oku shares c.60% basic vocabulary with Yareban languages.

sources.note: Nothing. Index: 'O'oku -- Earlier reference to what is now regarded as probably part of YAREBA'; YAREBA entry lists O'oku? among possible dialects.
